item.title: Multimodal Large Language Models and Agentic AI in Transportation
item.content:encoded:
Yuhuan Lu, Macao Polytechnic University

Yuanfang Zhu, Nagoya University

Jun Zhuang, Boise State University

Guoqiang Mao, Southeast University

This special issue addresses how multimodal large language models and agentic AI are transforming transportation systems. By combining language understanding with visual, spatial, and sensor data, these technologies enable more intelligent autonomous driving, traffic management, and mobility services. The focus is on advancing safety, efficiency, accessibility, and sustainability across transportation networks.

The issue tackles key challenges in deploying these systems in transportation, including grounding language in real traffic scenes, handling diverse sensor inputs, generalizing across different cities and conditions, and ensuring trustworthy decision-making in safety-critical scenarios. Submissions should connect foundational AI methods to rigorous evaluation and real-world transportation outcomes.

The special issue welcomes research on architectures, algorithms, datasets, benchmarks, and deployment of multimodal and LLM-based systems across autonomous driving, traffic prediction, infrastructure coordination, public transit, and freight logistics. Research addressing safety, fairness, privacy, human oversight, and sustainability in transportation AI is also welcomed.

item.title: Safe and Trustworthy Autonomous Systems in Real-World Environments
item.content:encoded:
Heye Huang, Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST)

Inhi Kim, Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST)

Boqi Li, Beihang University

Haotian Shi, Tongji University

Lei Yang, Nanyang Technological University

Kailai Sun, Massachusetts Institute of Technology

Autonomous systems operating in complex real-world environments face significant challenges in ensuring safety, reliability, and generalization. This special issue seeks research that advances trustworthy autonomy through integration of data-driven learning with structured knowledge, world models, formal verification, and uncertainty reasoning. Contributions should address both average-case and long-tail safety-critical scenarios, with emphasis on how autonomous systems can identify risks, adapt continually, and coordinate with other agents.

The scope includes autonomous vehicles, robotics, embodied AI, and other safety-critical platforms. Submissions may combine learning, optimization, control, simulation, and human-centered methods provided they clearly contribute to trustworthy autonomous behavior. The issue welcomes original research, reviews, benchmarks, and perspective articles demonstrating methodological novelty, rigorous evaluation, or insights transferable to real-world autonomous system deployment.

item.title: Multimodal Learning for Embodied Intelligence: Perception, Alignment, Fusion, Reasoning, and Generation
item.content:encoded:
Zhiliang Wu, Nanyang Technological University

Kun Li, United Arab Emirates University

Yunqiu Xu, National University of Singapore

Embodied intelligence systems must integrate diverse sensory inputs—vision, language, audio, touch, 3D signals, and action trajectories—to perceive and act in the physical world. This special issue focuses on multimodal learning approaches that enable embodied agents to build effective world models from these heterogeneous inputs. The work addresses unique challenges in embodied settings, including spatiotemporal understanding, cross-modal fusion, causal reasoning, and handling real-world conditions like noise, missing data, and partial observability.

The special issue invites research on multimodal representation learning, information fusion, and reasoning methods for embodied systems. Studies should explore how embodied agents leverage foundation models and integrate multiple modalities for tasks ranging from perception and interaction to planning, decision-making, and world model generation.

The challenge of creating accurate and generalizable AI systems in complex operating conditions motivates the inclusion of domain knowledge directly into learning architectures, combining data-driven approaches with established engineering principles.

item.title: Physical Machine Learning and Large Language Models for Remote Sensing and Earth Observation
item.content:encoded:
Wenchao Zhang, Xi'an University of Science and Technology

Yongze Song, Curtin University

Jiaxin Li, Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

Remote sensing and Earth observation are advancing through integration of multi-source satellite and UAV data with machine learning and large language models. Physical machine learning—combining physics knowledge with data-driven approaches through physics-informed constraints and neural operators—enhances consistency and generalization. Geospatial foundation models and multimodal language systems enable knowledge transfer across sensors and support open-vocabulary perception and reasoning.

This special issue seeks original research on physics-informed learning, geospatial foundation models, and language-based intelligence for remote sensing applications. Submissions should advance methodological approaches, establish benchmarks, or demonstrate applications that improve accuracy, generalization, interpretability, and operational value across environmental monitoring, resource management, and disaster response. Studies combining these complementary approaches are particularly encouraged.

item.title: Computer Applications Frontiers: Opportunities, Challenges, Technologies and Applications
item.content:encoded:
Xiaoou Ding, Harbin Institute of Technology

Kaiyu Li, Wilfrid Laurier University

This special issue focuses on advanced computer application technologies such as AI, Big Data, Large Models, Blockchain, IoT, Cloud Computing, 5G, and Digital Twins, and their integration across various industries. A key challenge is building efficient, secure, and intelligent systems that enable interoperability between industrial equipment, information systems, business processes, and enterprise services.

The issue seeks original research and review papers that address technical challenges and explore how intelligent methods and self-adaptive models can provide solutions relevant to dynamic engineering environments, particularly in fields like transportation and environmental engineering where conditions change rapidly.

The special issue aims to assess the current state of the art in using advanced computer applications to tackle complex interoperability challenges, identify knowledge gaps, and propose future research directions for both academia and industry.

item.title: Human-Robot Interaction (HRI) and Social Robots
item.content:encoded:
Patrick C. K Hung, Ontario Tech University

Sangseok You, Sungkyunkwan University (SKKU)

This special issue addresses social robots and human-robot interaction (HRI), exploring how physical robots integrated with network infrastructure and cloud services interact with humans. The collection examines how concepts like the Uncanny Valley theory influence robot design, particularly regarding anthropomorphic and zoomorphic features that help robots gain user trust through emotional expression, gesture, and speech recognition.

The issue emphasizes the critical role of artificial intelligence technologies, including generative AI and machine learning, in enabling advanced social robot capabilities. It seeks interdisciplinary contributions spanning social science, computer science, decision science, and information systems, with emphasis on practical applications in healthcare, education, entertainment, and other domains.

item.title: LLMs and Agentic AI in Healthcare
item.content:encoded:
Malek Masmoudi, University of Sharjah

Patrick Siarry, Université Paris-Est Créteil

Omar Tujjar, International Society of Medical AI (ISMAI)

This special issue focuses on the integration of large language models and agentic AI systems in healthcare. The issue invites research on how these autonomous, reasoning-capable technologies can transform clinical practice, hospital operations, and healthcare management while promoting patient-centered care and sustainability.

Healthcare organizations increasingly deploy AI agents that combine perception of diverse clinical data with capabilities like planning, tool use, and collaboration to support clinicians, patients, researchers, and administrators. As adoption grows, rigorous evaluation and trustworthiness become critical to ensure these systems remain safe, auditable, and aligned with clinical standards.

The special issue welcomes original research articles, position papers, and validated case studies on both technical topics such as architectures and algorithms, and socio-technical topics including ethics, policy, and human factors across all stages of agentic AI deployment in healthcare.
